newsitem.title: THAILAND: INTERVIEW - Furukawa Metal awaits end-Jan listing.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Furukawa Metal awaits end-Jan listing.

text.p: Furukawa Metal (Thailand) Plc, a unit of Furukawa Electric Co Ltd, said on Tuesday it expects to make a successful debut on the Thai stock exchange by the end of this month.

Chai Sophonpanich, chairman of the major copper tube producer, told Reuters in an interview that the firms shares would unlikely trade below its initial public offering price of 45 baht ($1.80) and should make a good long-term investment.

"We hope that the price we come up with will be attractive enough to get buyers...we sold a bit cheap to make sure that the chance of buyers losing money is minimal," he said. "Moreover we are coming out at a time when the market is bottoming out."
Furukawa in November floated 14.5 million share at 45 baht ($1.8) each. A total of 7.4 million shares will be offered to local investors and the rest to foreign investors.

The company raised 652.5 million baht from the offering to fund its 980-million-baht expansion project. The expansion will raise production capacity to 18,000 tonnes during the first quarter of 1997 from the current 10,560 tonnes.
The company is now awaiting the green light from the stock exchange to trade.
Chai said he was bullish about the fundamentals and outlook for Furukawa Metal whose copper tubes are used in the manufacture of air-conditioners and refrigerators.
He expected the firm's 1996 net profit to be better than the forecast of 219 million baht as the half year profit had already reached 150 million baht.
"That is a rather conservative forecast," he said.
Chai said growth in 1997 would be slower than in 1996 due to start-up costs following the expansion but he expressed confidence that earnings growth would improve in 1998.
The increased capacity was expected to raise the firm's Thai market share to 47 percent from 42-43 percent currently, he said.
There are only two seamless copper tube producers in Thailand at present -- Furukawa Metal and Bangkok Metal Industry with 25 percent market share. The rest is imported.
Furukawa metal sells 85 percent of its products to Thailand-based refrigerators and air-conditioners manufacturers and exporters and exports the rest.
Chai said despite Thailand's sluggish export growth in 1996, the demand for refrigerators and air-conditioners in the global market was still high.
Analysts forecast that the production of the two cooling products in Thailand was expected to reach 8.6 units in 2000 from 5.5 million units estimated in 1996.
